answer:
The Atlas Logistics pilot (8-week, 80 users across dispatch and warehouse teams) was highly successful, meeting or exceeding every benchmark. Measured results: weekly active usage was 87.5% vs >75% target; query success rate 84.2% vs >80%; citation accuracy 88.6% vs >85% (improved from 74% in March to 88.6% in April after the April 15 citation validation update); median onboarding duration 4.8 weeks vs 5.0-week target (down from 6.0-week historical average); support escalations declined 18.4% vs >15%; and average query latency was 1.8 seconds vs <2.0-second target [NL-020#NL-020-S04].

Key lessons from the pilot: pre-ingestion document cleanup is the most effective way to prevent citation errors and should be mandatory for all onboarding; mid-market clients should keep permissions simple with broad department-level folders; and frontline teams need mobile-friendly UI and messaging integrations because a standard web browser is not ideal for floor staff [NL-020#NL-020-S07].

The expansion recommendation is to proceed with a phased company-wide rollout: Phase 1 (Q3 2026) expands Growth Plan active users from 80 to 500 across Chicago, Dallas, and Atlanta with a $2,500 onboarding fee and two training webinars; Phase 2 (August 2026) transitions Atlas to the advanced OCR ingestion pipeline for legacy scanned documents; Phase 3 (Q4 2026) moves Atlas to the Enterprise Plan (starting at $8,500/month) if users exceed the 2,000 Growth Plan limit, including adding ~1,500 delivery drivers and deploying the Microsoft Teams integration; Phase 4 (Q1 2027) establishes an automated API data pipeline between Atlas's dispatch database and NovaLearn's KnowledgeHub, plus automated query audit scripts and quarterly compliance reports [NL-020#NL-020-S08].
